title: Optimize NCCL overlap for tensor-parallel collectives with kernel-aware scheduling and KV-cache hints
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Performance: Improved end-to-end throughput and 10-30% lower p95 latency for TP collectives on 8xA100 and 16xH100 clusters when running long-context workloads; safe rollout default enabled for Dedicated clusters.
description: Motivation: Tensor-parallel workloads were seeing suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and local kernel execution for mixed KV-cache + generation traffic. This caused higher p95 latency and reduced throughput on longer context sequences. This PR introduces a set of coordinated changes: 1) NCCL stream priority tuning and explicit stream affinity for collective ops to reduce head-of-line blocking; 2) a lightweight kernel-aware scheduler that assigns compute kernels to streams based on predicted device occupancy and pending collective sizes; 3) KV-cache hinting so the scheduler delays inexpensive KV cache maintenance work onto low-priority streams and avoids stalling collective-critical streams; 4) smaller scheduling and batching heuristics to improve continuous-batching latency tail without regressions in average throughput. The description below is a single continuous string. Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1983/tp-nccl-overlap-design. Checklist: - [x] microbenchmarks (local and CI perf) - [x] integration tests with rpctest harness - [x] backward-compatible API and config flags - [x] docs and runbook updates - [x] staged rollout plan for Dedicated clusters (ENG-2040). Backwards compatibility: Changes are opt-in via runtime config flags; default rollout enabled for internal Dedicated and can be toggled by ops. Impact: Measured improvements vary by model and hardware; in our perf lab we observed 10-30% p95 latency improvement and 8-18% throughput uplift on long-context runs on 8xA100 and 16xH100 evaluation clusters. Safety: Added feature flags and metrics to monitor overlap efficiency; automatic rollback on sustained error or latency regression. Related work: follow-ups from pr-41567 and pr-40312 which adjusted stream priorities and kernel scheduling heuristics. CI summary: some flaky perf checks required a rerun (see review comments).

review_comments: Daniel Kim: LGTM overall, but please add a comment explaining the choice of default low/high stream priorities and a pointer to the NCCL doc we referenced.
Aisha Patel (author): Added inline comments and link to NCCL stream priority notes in nccl_stream_manager.h, clarified default mapping rationale.
Sana Rivera: We observed a flaky test in perf pipeline (tp_overlap_bench) that timed out on 16xH100. Can you add a retry and increase timeouts for long-context runs?
Aisha Patel: Increased timeout and added deterministic seed to the perf harness; retriggered CI. Perf flakiness resolved after rerun.
Marco Li: Can we expose a runtime config to disable KV-cache hinting for workloads sensitive to memory ordering? Consider adding a diagnostic metric for skipped hints.
Aisha Patel: Added runtime flag runtime.tp.enable_kv_hinting (default true) and metric tp_kv_hint_skipped_count. Updated docs with rollout instructions.
